metadata.notes: agent_supports: yes — two `hermes chat` REPLs run concurrently in one cwd (verified live). daemon_capability: full — the cwd fallback's guard is per DISTINCT cwd, not per process, so a same-cwd pair resolves and claim-aware disambiguation gives each session its own PID. driver_capability: gap:start_session — start_session/session are not_implemented stubs and the turn counter is global.

assessment.body:
## Verdict

agent_supports: yes
daemon_capability: full
driver_capability: gap:start_session

## agent — yes

`hermes chat` is an ordinary interactive REPL with no per-directory or
per-machine singleton: two of them launch side by side in one cwd. Verified
live on v0.19.0 rather than argued: two concurrent hermes session processes ran
in a single directory at the same time (`pgrep -f` output cited in sources),
and the maintainer's own store already contains same-second concurrent pairs
from earlier runs (`20260802_212608_1dc71a` / `20260802_212608_feed91`, two
distinct ids, `started_at` 0.017 s apart). Each session gets its own
`sessions` row with its own id, `started_at`, token counters and
`finish_reason` stream, so "two distinct session_ids with independent arcs" is
a property of the store, not something the adapter has to synthesise.

## daemon — full

The scenario's four observables are (1) two distinct session rows, (2) distinct
PIDs, (3) independent state arcs, (4) a stable PID-to-session binding.

**(1) and (3) are free.** The watcher keys its cursor on the store's session id
(`watcher.go` `sessions map[string]*sessionCursor`), scans
`source IN ('cli','tui')` rows and emits `new_session` + `activity` per id;
`turnIsDone` reads `finish_reason='stop'` off *that session's* newest message
row. Nothing in that path is shared between two sessions, so a turn in one
cannot move the other. The messaging-gateway rows that share the table are
filtered out by the `source` predicate.

**(2) and (4) hinge on cwd — and this scenario is the case the cwd fallback
actually handles.** `sessions.cwd` is NULL for `source='cli'` rows (only
Hermes' `tui_gateway/server.py` ever calls `update_session_cwd` — grep cited
below), so the adapter falls back to `defaultLiveCWD`. The prerequisite every
other assessed hermes cell carries — "exactly one live hermes session
process" — is stricter than the code: `defaultLiveCWD` bails on
`len(cwds) != 1` where `cwds` comes from
`processlifecycle.LiveCWDsByCmdline`, which returns a **set of directories**
(`set[dir] = struct{}{}`), not a list of PIDs. Two session processes sharing
ONE directory collapse to a single set entry, so the guard passes and the
fallback returns that directory. This cell is same-cwd by definition, so it
satisfies the guard *by construction*.

Verified live rather than read off the code: with two `hermes chat --tui`
processes running in `/private/tmp/hermes41probe`, `pgrep -f` with the
adapter's exact `processCmdPattern` matched exactly three PIDs — the two
session processes (both `cwd=/private/tmp/hermes41probe`) and the long-lived
`python -m hermes_cli.main gateway run --replace`, which `isServiceArgv`
excludes (`gateway` is in `serviceSubcommands`) and which `LiveCWDsByCmdline`
therefore never contributes its own `~/.hermes` cwd from. The two child
processes each session spawns — the Node TUI (`ui-tui/dist/entry.js`) and
`python3 -m tui_gateway.entry` — do NOT match the pattern (`/hermes` must be
followed by a space or end-of-string; `hermes-agent/`, `.hermes/` and
`hermes-local/` all fail that bound), so they cannot pollute the candidate set
either. Candidate set = exactly the two session processes = exactly what this
scenario wants.

From a non-empty shared cwd the rest follows the claudecode path that is
already recorded and verified for this scenario:

- `DiscoverPID` → `DiscoverPIDByCWDAndCmdLineExcludingArgv` finds both PIDs at
  that cwd and hands them to `PIDManager.claimAwareDisambiguate`, which prefers
  the highest **unclaimed** PID — so the second session cannot be handed the
  PID the first already claimed. Distinct PIDs, and a claimed PID is never
  re-disambiguated, which is criterion (4).
- The mapping is not merely distinct but *correct* under the recipe's
  sequential order: session 1's store row is INSERTed on its first user
  message, ~2 s in, while its process is still the only one alive — an
  unambiguous bind — and session 2's row then takes the only remaining
  unclaimed PID.
- The two `proc-<PID>` pre-sessions the process scanner mints retire cleanly:
  `findSupersedingSession` matches on `proc.PID == candidate.PID` once each
  real session binds its PID, so the row count settles at two, not four.

No spec-required observable is mis-handled on the recipe this cell specifies,
so the verdict is `full`.

### What the daemon genuinely cannot do (out of scope here, cited so it is not
re-litigated)

If a hermes session process is alive in a *different* directory during the
recording, the set has two entries, `defaultLiveCWD` returns "", and then:
both store sessions get `CWD=""`; `DiscoverPIDByCWDAndCmdLineExcludingArgv`
short-circuits on `cwd == ""` and binds no PID at all; and the pre-sessions
never retire, because `findSupersedingSession` needs either a PID match (the
real sessions have PID 0) or `proc.CWD == candidate.CWD` (the real sessions
have ""), so `cleanupPreSessionsForProject` — matching on `projectDir`, also
empty — misses them too. Four rows, two of them PID-less, forever.

Is that a fixable daemon gap or genuinely unobservable? Both, depending on
surface and config, and this is the honest split:

- **TUI surface: fixable today, no daemon change needed.** `hermes chat --tui`
  writes `source='tui'` with `cwd` POPULATED (dispatcher's live probe;
  independently consistent with `update_session_cwd` being called only from
  `tui_gateway/server.py`). Both `scanSessions` (`cwd = r.cwd`, fallback only
  when empty, `anyRowNeedsCWD` never even consults the live probe) and
  `querySessionMetrics` (`lastCWD := cwd.String`) prefer the stored value, so
  two concurrent TUI sessions bind their own cwd from their own row with no
  ambiguity guard involved at all.
- **CLI surface: conditionally fixable, not by inference.** The store persists
  no pid, tty or cwd for `source='cli'` (full `PRAGMA table_info(sessions)`
  cited below — 48 columns, none process-related), so no query can link a
  session id to a process. Hermes does keep an explicit
  pid↔session_id registry — `$HERMES_HOME/runtime/active_sessions.json`,
  entries `{lease_id, session_id, surface, pid, process_start_time, started_at,
  updated_at}` — but `try_acquire_active_session` returns a no-op lease and
  writes NOTHING when `max_concurrent_sessions` is unset, which is the default:
  no `runtime/` directory exists in either hermes home on this machine. So a
  per-PID binding is implementable only for users who opt into a session cap.
- **Time-correlation is not a fix.** The one remaining discriminator —
  `sessions.started_at` vs process start time — is a coin flip in exactly the
  case that needs it: the store's existing concurrent pair is 0.017 s apart.

None of that is triggered by this cell's recipe, so it lives here and in
`caveats`, not in the verdict (caveats-over-downgrades).

## driver — gap:start_session

`replaydata/agents/hermes/driver-interactive.sh` declares
`DRIVE_ELICITS="send slash sleep wait_turn"`; `start_session` and `session` are
both `not_implemented` stub arms, and the recipe needs both (launch the second
REPL without tearing the first down, then route the third turn back to slot 1).
Two further seams must be made slot-aware in the same port, and neither is
visible from the step-type list:

1. `EXPECTED_TURNS_SEEN` is a single **global** counter. With two slots,
   session 2's `wait_turn` compares session 2's stop-count (1) against the
   global counter session 1 already advanced to 1 and spins to the deadline.
   The slot array `SES_EXPECTED[]` is already declared for exactly this — the
   port is to use `SES_EXPECTED[$ACTIVE]`.
2. `resolve_session_id` binds "newest `cli|tui` row with
   `started_at > SES_LAUNCH_TS[$ACTIVE]`". That is correct per slot only if
   slot 1 is resolved before slot 2's row exists; the recipe's sequential order
   guarantees it, but the port should keep the per-slot launch timestamp
   comparison rather than a global "newest row".

This is tooling work, not an observability limit, so the cell keeps its full
recipe and spec and routes `driver-gap`.

## Provisional

Everything above is code, live process inspection and live store queries — no
hermes recording exists yet for any cell. The two things only a recording can
settle: whether the pre-session→store-session supersession really lands
cleanly for BOTH sessions (the PID-match path is what makes it work, and it has
never been exercised with two concurrent hermes rows), and whether the
claim-aware bind assigns session 1 the process that actually wrote it — the
verify vector cannot see a swapped mapping, so it would pass either way. Hence
confidence 0.8.
caveats: The 'exactly one live hermes process' prerequisite copied into every other assessed hermes cell is stricter than the code: defaultLiveCWD guards on the number of DISTINCT cwds (LiveCWDsByCmdline returns map[dir]struct{}), not the number of processes. This cell is safe with two processes precisely because they share one directory. The real prerequisite — here and, on re-read, in the sibling cells — is 'no hermes session process alive in a DIFFERENT cwd'.

A swapped PID-to-session mapping is INVISIBLE to this spec. The verify vector asserts distinct ids and independent arcs, both of which come from the store and are correct regardless of which process each row is bound to. The recipe's sequential order (drive session 1 fully before launching session 2) is what makes the mapping correct by construction; a recipe that launched both up front would still verify green with the two bindings crossed.
PROVISIONAL daemon verdict: no hermes recording exists for any cell yet. The pre-session→store-session supersession by PID match has never run with two concurrent hermes sessions.

TUI surface is the hardening fallback, not a requirement: `hermes chat --tui` records source='tui' with sessions.cwd populated, which removes the live-process fallback from the picture entirely. It is NOT used here because it would add gap:tui_launch (already the driver verdict on cell 2-15) plus a Node/TUI-bundle prerequisite, for a cell the CLI surface already covers. If a recording shows cwd binding trouble, switching the launch seam to --tui is the fix — and the cwd then comes from each session's own row.

Cost is priced by irrlicht's capacity table, not read from the store: Hermes reports estimated_cost_usd=0.0 under billing_mode='subscription_included'. cost_nonzero therefore holds only while the model resolves in capacity/aliases.go (gpt-5.6-luna does, via the gpt-5 family).

The store row is INSERTed lazily, ~2s after the first user message, and the REPL itself takes several seconds to boot (the driver polls for 'Type your message or /help' with a 60s ceiling). Phase budgets are sized for that: 60s to the first working transition, 60s from session 1's first turn to session 2's.

sources.note: defaultLiveCWD: bails on len(cwds) != 1 where cwds is the SET returned by LiveCWDsByCmdline — a per-DISTINCT-CWD guard, not per-process. Two sessions in one cwd collapse to one entry and the fallback resolves. Also: per-session-id sessionCursor, scanSessions source filter, turnIsDone finish_reason='stop', per-row cwd preferred over fallbackCWD (reconcile: cwd := r.cwd; if cwd == "" { cwd = fallbackCWD }).
LiveCWDsByCmdline builds set := make(map[string]struct{}) keyed by directory, applies ExcludeArgv and skips the daemon's own PID — the set semantics that make this scenario observable.

DiscoverPIDByCWDAndCmdLineExcludingArgv returns (0, nil) immediately when cwd == "" (the failure mode when two DIFFERENT cwds are live); narrowByCWD hands multiple same-cwd matches to the caller's disambiguator.
claimAwareDisambiguate prefers the highest UNCLAIMED PID, falling back to the highest claimed — so two same-cwd sessions cannot be bound to the same PID.

findSupersedingSession: matchPID (real session PID == proc-<PID>) retires the pre-session with no grace; the matchCWD fallback requires proc.CWD != "" and an equal candidate.CWD — which is why a PID-less, cwd-less real session leaves its pre-session stranded.
cleanupPreSessionsForProject matches pre-sessions by projectDir, then by realCWD — both empty for a cwd-less hermes store session, which is the other half of the stranded-ghost failure mode.

hermes gets its store watcher PLUS a processlifecycle.Scanner keyed on the CommandPattern, with ExcludeArgv as the scanner's argv filter — the source of the two proc-<PID> pre-sessions this cell has to see retired.

pgrep -f '(^|/)hermes( |$)|hermes_cli\.main' matched exactly 3 PIDs: 75303 and 75894 (the two session processes, both cwd=/private/tmp/hermes41probe) and 11108 (`python -m hermes_cli.main gateway run --replace`, cwd=~/.hermes, excluded by isServiceArgv). The per-session children — `node --expose-gc .../ui-tui/dist/entry.js` and `python3 -m tui_gateway.entry` — did NOT match the pattern. Probe sent no prompt; the store's session count was 25 before and after.

48 columns (id, source, user_id, session_key, chat_id, …, cwd, git_branch, git_repo_root, billing_*, …, archived, pinned). NONE is a pid, tty, or process identifier — grep for pid|proc|tty|host returns nothing. The store cannot link a session id to a process.

Ten most recent cli rows: all source='cli', cwd EMPTY, model='gpt-5.6-luna'. Includes concurrent pairs 0.017s apart (20260802_212608_1dc71a / _feed91, and two more pairs) — evidence both that concurrent sessions are ordinary for this agent and that started_at cannot discriminate them.
Every caller of update_session_cwd lives in the TUI gateway — the primary-source confirmation that source='cli' rows carry no cwd and source='tui' rows do.

try_acquire_active_session writes {lease_id, session_id, surface, pid, process_start_time, started_at, updated_at} to $HERMES_HOME/runtime/active_sessions.json — an explicit pid↔session_id map — but ONLY when max_concurrent_sessions resolves; otherwise it returns an enabled=False no-op lease and writes nothing. Verified: no runtime/ directory exists in either hermes home here, so the registry is absent under default config.

DRIVE_ELICITS="send slash sleep wait_turn"; start_session and session are not_implemented stubs; EXPECTED_TURNS_SEEN is a single global counter (SES_EXPECTED[] is declared but unused); resolve_session_id binds the newest cli|tui row started after SES_LAUNCH_TS[$ACTIVE].

Recorded and verified sibling for this scenario: the recipe shape (turn → start_session → turn → {"session":1} turn) and the working-anchored spec this cell mirrors, including its reason for anchoring on working rather than ready (the proc-<PID> pre-session is born ready and never enters working).
Upstream project. Local CLI reports 'Hermes Agent v0.19.0 (2026.7.20) · upstream d0b87dad'.

preconditions: hermes >=0.19.0 on PATH with an inference provider configured in <HERMES_HOME>/config.yaml and working credentials
HERMES_HOME exported in the shell that runs run-cell.sh, so the recording daemon (which inherits it) and the driver read the same state.db
sqlite3 on PATH — the store is the only session signal hermes exposes; the driver exits nonzero(2) without it

NO hermes session process alive in a DIFFERENT cwd. Two processes in the SAME cwd are fine and are the point of this cell: defaultLiveCWD guards on the number of distinct cwds, not the number of processes. A hermes session running elsewhere makes the set size 2, the fallback returns "", and BOTH sessions land with no cwd and no PID. The long-lived `hermes gateway run` service is exempt — isServiceArgv excludes it before the set is built.
irrlichd is recording with the hermes 'store' observe permission granted (grant-all permission mode)
setup: Driver auto-starts session 1 (slot 1) via launch_repl in <staging>/cwd, waits for the 'Type your message or /help' banner, and resolves its store id after the first send

PORT REQUIRED (this is the gap:start_session verdict): the start_session arm must save_active, alloc_slot with the SAME RUN_CWD, and launch a second `hermes chat` under tmux while slot 1 stays alive; the session arm must save_active + load_slot N so a step carrying {"session":1} routes back to slot 1

PORT REQUIRED: make the turn counter per-slot — replace the global EXPECTED_TURNS_SEEN with the already-declared SES_EXPECTED[$ACTIVE], or session 2's wait_turn compares against session 1's count and spins to the deadline
PORT REQUIRED: keep resolve_session_id's per-slot `started_at > SES_LAUNCH_TS[$ACTIVE]` filter; a global 'newest row' would bind slot 2's id to slot 1 once both sessions exist

Keep the order sequential — session 1 completes a turn BEFORE session 2 launches — so session 1's store row binds its PID while its process is the only one alive; that is what makes the PID mapping correct rather than merely distinct

script.text: Reply with exactly the word: alpha
Reply with exactly the word: bravo
Reply with exactly the word: alpha2

verify: events.jsonl contains 2 distinct store-backed session_ids (<YYYYMMDD>_<HHMMSS>_<hex>), both with the same cwd
each id has its own working->ready arc; no transition on one id is attributed to the other
session 1 shows TWO working->ready arcs (turn 1 + the post-start_session re-drive), session 2 shows ONE
both sessions carry a non-zero PID and the two PIDs differ; neither binding changes after it is first assigned
both proc-<PID> pre-sessions are retired — the final row count for this cwd is 2, not 4
the store rows are source='cli' (the CLI surface this recipe drives), each with its own token counters
